Schnakenberg Model

Radial-only patterns with genuine steady state

Overview

The Schnakenberg model is a minimal two-component activator-inhibitor system closely related to the Brusselator but with simpler kinetics. When coupled to diffusiophoresis, it produces radial/concentric patterns only, similar to Gray-Scott and fundamentally different from Brusselator and FHN.

WarningKey Finding: Radial Symmetry Only

Schnakenberg produces concentric ring patterns regardless of gamma (200-1000) or multi-type configurations. No hexagonal symmetry breaking occurs. This confirms a clear dichotomy: cubic autocatalysis (Brusselator) or excitable dynamics (FHN) are required for hexagonal mode.

Mathematical Formulation

The Schnakenberg reaction-diffusion system:

\[ \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = D_u \nabla^2 u + \gamma(a - u + u^2 v) \]

\[ \frac{\partial v}{\partial t} = D_v \nabla^2 v + \gamma(b - u^2 v) \]

Where:

  • \(u\): Activator concentration
  • \(v\): Inhibitor concentration
  • \(D_u, D_v\): Diffusion coefficients (\(D_v \gg D_u\) for Turing instability)
  • \(a, b\): Kinetic parameters
  • \(\gamma\): Reaction rate scaling (Damkohler-like)

Turing Analysis

The homogeneous steady state is: \[ u^* = a + b, \quad v^* = \frac{b}{(a+b)^2} \]

Turing instability requires \(D_v/D_u\) sufficiently large and \(\gamma\) above a critical threshold.

Parameters

Symbol Description Tested Range
\(D_u\) Activator diffusion 0.015
\(D_v\) Inhibitor diffusion 0.15
\(a\) Feed parameter 0.1
\(b\) Feed parameter 0.9
\(\gamma\) Reaction rate 200-1000

NoteUnique Property: Genuine Steady State

Schnakenberg achieves a genuine plateau (0.62 at gamma=200), unlike all other tested models where patterns remain dynamic. This steady-state convergence is unique among the four PDE variants.

Key Observations

  • Radial patterns only: Concentric rings regardless of gamma, particle types, or initial conditions
  • No hexagonal breaking: Extended simulation confirms radial symmetry persists
  • Steady state: Plateau=0.62 (unique — Brusselator/FHN/Gray-Scott all have plateau~0)
  • Simple kinetics: Fewer parameters than Brusselator, but also fewer accessible morphologies

Comparison: Four-Model Hierarchy

Model Symmetry Breaking Accessible Modes Steady State
Brusselator Yes Hexagonal, Stripes, Labyrinth No (dynamic)
FitzHugh-Nagumo Yes Hexagonal, Square/Grid No (oscillatory)
Schnakenberg No Radial only Yes (plateau=0.62)
Gray-Scott No Radial only No (dynamic)
